market.audience: US families in the first weeks after a birth who need to know what applies, when it closes, and what to bring
market.problem: Generic checklists omit state, household, insurance, and parentage details, turning one urgent deadline into a pile of tabs and handouts.
market.advantage: Baby Docs builds from the family's answers, then shows the deadlines, official sources, and document checklists that fit that household on one device.
market.competitive_context: The app competes with generic newborn checklists, hospital handouts, and calendar reminders. It wins on personal applicability and source-backed tasks, while staying on-device and never filing anything for the family.

proof_points.claim: The plan screen puts the next hard deadline and open work in one ordered view.
The task detail screen explains why the task applies, what timing means, and where the official office is.
The Plus surface shows the on-device document vault as work around the free deadline and checklist surfaces.
